content: TechSpot/TheHackerNews/Malwarebytes/CyberInsider (Aug 2025) corroborate: 1Password, Bitwarden, LastPass, Enpass, iCloud Passwords, LogMeOnce extensions vulnerable to DOM-based clickjacking (Marek Toth). Bitwarden shipped a fix in 2025.8.0; 1Password fixed in 8.11.7 after initially triaging as 'informative'/out of scope. PoCs demonstrated theft of stored credit-card data, PII, login credentials, and TOTP codes via sites with an existing XSS or subdomain issue combined with the clickjacking chain. This is the direct, current, real-world precedent for why an in-page (DOM-resident) credential-adjacent UI is a live, recently-exploited risk class, not a theoretical one.
